limitations: The catalog names no third-party project. Every profile is an original description of a tool category, with licence 'unverified', no homepage and no tested Windows builds, CPU architectures or tool version. Real listings need a person to verify the licence, pin a version and record reversal steps (gate G5).
Compatibility cannot return 'compatible' for any shipped profile, because nothing has been tested. Off Windows it returns 'incompatible'. Before the system is loaded it returns 'unknown'.

SystemInfo has no Windows build number, so build-range checks report 'unknown' until the native owner adds a build field. Pass windowsBuild through checkCompatibility's environment argument once that exists; the component currently passes null.

All five preference effects are marked unsupported and rendered disabled with their reason. No adapter exists, so previews never change a Windows setting, and the export always records appliesToWindows: false.

Preferences are saved through usePref under localStorage key 'jarvis.ui.customization' (UI-only, non-sensitive, validated on read). The export is a user-initiated JSON download using an anchor with a blob URL. Electron has no will-download handler in this repo, so the save location and prompt come from Electron defaults and were not verified in the desktop app.
Restore (roadmap 75 import) is not built and its button is disabled. Roadmap 76-80 are listed as not built and have no controls.
The component is not wired into App.tsx or any navigation. The captain must add the route and pass the system prop.

Visual layout was not checked in the Electron window. Verification is the unit tests and a static-markup render of the real component in Node, which checks text, disabled states and labels, not pixels.
No copied third-party code, GPL/AGPL material or dependency was added. The only imports are the existing repo modules, React primitives and the existing icon package.
